_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from Soft Serve's documentation; no upstream egg.
name: Soft Serve
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Soft Serve is a self-hostable Git server for the command line: browse, clone and push repositories over SSH. The egg runs it with SQLite, makes your SSH key the admin's, and keeps repositories private unless you open them.
startup: export SOFT_SERVE_DATA_PATH=/home/container/data; if [ ! -f data/soft-serve.db ] && [ -z "{{ADMIN_KEYS}}" ]; then echo "Set Admin SSH keys first: without one, nobody could manage Soft Serve."; exit 1; fi; [ -n "{{ADMIN_KEYS}}" ] && export SOFT_SERVE_INITIAL_ADMIN_KEYS="{{ADMIN_KEYS}}"; h="{{PUBLIC_HOST}}"; h=${h:-$SERVER_IP}; h=${h:-localhost}; SOFT_SERVE_NAME="{{SERVER_NAME}}" SOFT_SERVE_ANON_ACCESS={{ANON_ACCESS}} SOFT_SERVE_SSH_LISTEN_ADDR=:{{SERVER_PORT}} SOFT_SERVE_SSH_PUBLIC_URL=ssh://$h:{{SERVER_PORT}} SOFT_SERVE_HTTP_ENABLED={{HTTP_ENABLED}} SOFT_SERVE_HTTP_LISTEN_ADDR=:{{HTTP_PORT}} SOFT_SERVE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL=http://$h:{{HTTP_PORT}} SOFT_SERVE_GIT_ENABLED=false SOFT_SERVE_STATS_ENABLED=false exec ./soft serve

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Soft Serve: downloads Soft Serve from its GitHub releases, checked
# against GitHub's SHA-256. Repositories, the database, keys and settings
# (the data folder) are never touched, and the binary is only replaced
# once the new one is complete.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x86_64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Soft Serve has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag charmbracelet/soft-serve "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x soft ] && [ "$(cat .soft-serve-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Soft Serve $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Soft Serve $tag"
    file="soft-serve_${tag#v}_Linux_${arch}.tar.gz"
    gh-release download charmbracelet/soft-serve "$tag" "$file" "$work/soft.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/soft.tar.gz" -C "$work"
    bin=$(find "$work" -type f -name soft | head -n 1)
    [ -n "$bin" ] || fail "Soft Serve's download didn't have the soft program. Reinstall to try again."
    install -m 0755 "$bin" soft.new
    mv -f soft.new soft
    echo "$tag" > .soft-serve-version
fi
mkdir -p data
echo "Installed Soft Serve $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Soft Serve version to install, such as 0.12.4, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Admin SSH keys
variables.description: Your SSH public key (such as ssh-ed25519 AAAA... you@laptop), made the admin's on the first start. More admins can be added over SSH later.

variables.name: Name
variables.description: The server's name, shown in its menu.

variables.name: Anonymous access
variables.description: What people without an account can do: no-access, read-only or read-write. Each repository can still be made public or private.

variables.name: Public address
variables.description: The host name or IP address shown in clone links. Empty uses the server's IP address.

variables.name: Git over HTTP
variables.description: Also serve Git over HTTP on its own port, added to the server first.

variables.name: HTTP port
variables.description: The port Git over HTTP listens on, when it's on.
